steps.name: ImportEnvironments
steps.label: Import Environments
steps.goal: Import every published environment on the project into the scene, homed under ENV/{asset}.
steps.pass_criteria: Each environment collection actually contains geometry (a mesh is linked in), not just an empty placeholder collection.
steps.fail_criteria: An env collection comes in empty (nothing linked), or a traceback.
steps.min_scenario: You dig through the project/library folders by hand to find the latest published version, confirm it's the right one, and bring it in — when the folders are tidy and it's where it should be.
steps.max_scenario: The published version isn't where it should be, is the wrong one, or was never published — you Slack/email whoever touched it last, wait, maybe walk the building, and the task stalls for days.

steps.name: ImportCharacterRigs
steps.label: Import Character Rigs
steps.goal: Find any character rigs on the show, import them, and lay them out on a grid so they don't stack on the origin and are easy to pick.
steps.pass_criteria: Every imported character sits in its own grid cell — no two characters share a world XY position (the layout applied).
steps.fail_criteria: Traceback, or two+ characters stacked on the same spot (placement skipped/broke, so the grid did not apply).
steps.min_scenario: You dig through the project/library folders by hand to find the latest published version, confirm it's the right one, and bring it in — when the folders are tidy and it's where it should be.
steps.max_scenario: The published version isn't where it should be, is the wrong one, or was never published — you Slack/email whoever touched it last, wait, maybe walk the building, and the task stalls for days.

steps.name: ImportStoryvisTimeline
steps.label: Import Storyvis Timeline
steps.goal: Import the storyvis timeline created in the alchemy scene editor.
steps.pass_criteria: the storyvis timeline is imported, all cameras are set up with image planes and appropriate audio.
steps.min_scenario: You dig through the project/library folders by hand to find the latest published version, confirm it's the right one, and bring it in — when the folders are tidy and it's where it should be.
steps.max_scenario: The published version isn't where it should be, is the wrong one, or was never published — you Slack/email whoever touched it last, wait, maybe walk the building, and the task stalls for days.

steps.name: ApplyLookdev
steps.label: Apply Lookdev
steps.goal: For every env and chr asset with a published ldv, append the UV-baked material into the scene and apply it to the asset's geometry mesh. Assets with no ldv data are skipped gracefully.
steps.pass_criteria: Every mesh that has a published ldv now carries its asset-specific material (not the grey default).
steps.fail_criteria: A material append failed or a mesh could not be found for an asset that has a valid ldv.
steps.min_scenario: All assets have published ldv with a materials_blend — one append + assign per asset.
steps.max_scenario: Some assets are missing ldv publishes or the materials blend has moved; manual material assignment required.

steps.name: ImportDesignModels
steps.label: Import Design Models
steps.goal: Bring each environment's high-detail design .glb (raw mesh-gen output from the dsn publish) into ENV_DSN/{asset}_dsn, scale-matched to the placed low-res env. This is the geometry the beauty render layer renders for a grounded style frame, while clay keeps the low-res silhouette. Also pins the scene to EEVEE.
steps.pass_criteria: Every env with a dsn .glb has a populated {asset}_dsn collection and the engine is EEVEE.
steps.fail_criteria: A dsn .glb exists but imported empty, or a traceback.
steps.min_scenario: Each env has a dsn publish with a .glb — one import + scale-match per asset.
steps.max_scenario: A dsn publish is missing its .glb or the env was never designed; manual import/placement required.

steps.name: SetPrevisRenderSettings
steps.label: Set Previs Render Settings
steps.goal: We're going to set the render to "Solid View" speficially planning on rendering out for a Seedance 2.0 render.  we're also going to set our outupt path per camera for the previs sequence.
steps.min_scenario: You set up the camera/settings and capture the media by hand, then drop it where reviewers look — when it works first try.
steps.max_scenario: Settings are off or reviewers can't find it; you re-capture and re-share, and review slips.

steps.name: SetUpCharacterMattes
steps.label: Set up Character Mattes
steps.goal: Set up matte passes for each character in the shot/sequence
steps.pass_criteria: Character matte passes are set up
steps.fail_criteria: Character matte passes are not set up.

steps.name: CleanRenderDir
steps.label: Clean Render Folder
steps.goal: Clear stale frames from the previs render folder before rendering, so a prior pass (wider frame range, a since-removed camera, old derived media) can't leave orphan data the player would mistake for the current render.
steps.pass_criteria: Render folder is clear of stale data for the shots about to render.
steps.fail_criteria: The render folder could not be cleaned.
steps.min_scenario: The previous pass's frames clear cleanly and the folder holds only what this pass will write.
steps.max_scenario: A file is locked or mis-pathed; you track down what's holding it and clear it by hand before re-rendering.

steps.name: SubmitRendersToDeadline
steps.label: Submit renders to deadline
steps.goal: Submit each shot for rendering on deadline.
steps.min_scenario: You set up the camera/settings and capture the media by hand, then drop it where reviewers look — when it works first try.
steps.max_scenario: Settings are off or reviewers can't find it; you re-capture and re-share, and review slips.

steps.name: CreatePrevisMovies
steps.label: Create Movie
steps.goal: Encode a review mp4 for each previs shot's rendered PNG sequence, landing each in the .preview convention so reviewers and the in-app player find it where they expect.
steps.pass_criteria: A preview mp4 exists for each rendered shot.
steps.min_scenario: The render sequences are on disk; you encode each shot to mp4 and drop it where reviewers look — when it works first try.
steps.max_scenario: Sequences are missing or mis-pathed; you re-render or re-path and re-encode, and review slips.
